questions.title: Vulnerable groups in medical research
questions.question: Vulnerable groups in medical research include those who are:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Having cancer does not itself impair the capacity to give free, informed consent; a diagnosis alone does not make a participant a vulnerable group in the consent-capacity sense.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Being immobile is a physical limitation that does not, by itself, impair decision-making capacity or the ability to consent to research.
explanations.C: Correct. The mentally ill are a vulnerable group in medical research because their illness can impair the capacity to give free and informed consent, so they need special protection against exploitation and coercion. Vulnerability here is about compromised autonomy and the ability to consent, not physical illness. This is why mentally ill participants, not the other groups listed, are classed as vulnerable.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A terminal illness does not necessarily remove decision-making capacity; being terminally ill does not by itself make a competent adult a vulnerable group in this sense.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the mentally ill as a vulnerable group in research because of impaired capacity to consent.

questions.hold: exact in-section duplicate of Q200 (vulnerable groups in research -> mentally ill; key C) — authored once as Q200
